content.intro: This lesson covers Introduction to WebAssembly. It sits in Module 26, WebAssembly and Cross-Platform Rust, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Introduction to WebAssembly matters when you work with portable modules and explicit host interfaces. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: WebAssembly provides a portable execution target, but browser or host access still depends on an explicit interface. Check target-specific toolchains, data conversion, and host permissions.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Introduction to WebAssembly, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. WebAssembly output runs inside a host environment with an explicit interface; producing a wasm artifact does not automatically grant browser, file, or network access.

content_blocks.run_instructions: For a real browser boundary, configure a supported wasm target and use a maintained binding tool if needed. The host defines which imports and exports are available.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Return the sample to its original form, run the documented command again, and compare the result. If a dependency, target, runtime, database, or hardware device is required, configure that separately before treating the result as verified.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake and recovery
content_blocks.text: Do not assume Introduction to WebAssembly guarantees more than it actually does. Reduce a failure to a small reproducer, read the full compiler diagnostic or error value, consult the matching official reference, and change one assumption at a time.

content_blocks.title: Toolchain and execution boundary
content_blocks.text: Course examples are static reference snippets, not executed inside CodeLeaf. Most standard-library examples can be tried in a Rust 2024 Cargo project; specialized networking, database, async, procedural-macro, embedded, and WebAssembly scenarios require the toolchain and dependencies described in their lessons.
